(By Smt. H.C.Lokeshwari, Advocate)
 :J U D G M E N T:
This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by her in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner is as follows:-
That on 26-05-2023, at about 9-30 P.M. the petitioner was traveling as a pillion rider in Dio Scooter bearing Reg.No.KA-05/KM-0706, on Thilak Nagara main road,
Bangalore and when they reached near K.G.Hospital, at that time, the driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-41/ME- 1910 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's motor cycle, result of which the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
3. Immediately she was shifted to K.G. Hospital, Bengaluru, Kunigal wherein admitted as an inpatient for 4 days.
So far the petitioner has spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards hospitalization, medical expenses and other incidental expenses etc.
Prior to the accident, the Petitioner was hale and healthy.
She was aged about 63 years and she was doing Coolie work and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m.
Due to the accidental injuries, petitioner is not in a position to do the said work and thereby petitioner and his entire family are put to great financial loss and mental agony.

4. The respondent no.1/ the RC owner of the car bearing Reg.No.KA-41-ME-1910 has filed written statement and admitted that he is the RC owner of the said car and same was insured with the respondent no.2 and the policy was in force as on the date of accident.

The respondent no.1 has further contended that the driver of the said car was not holding valid driving licence, hence they are not liable to pay any compensation in the even if the court holds that petitioner is entitled for compensation.

5. Respondent No.2/the Insurer of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-41/ME-1910 has filed the written statement and admitted the coverage of insurance policy and the liability if any subject to the terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.
The respondent no.2 has contended that the alleged accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent act on the part of the rider of the Dio Scooter.
There is no negligence on the part of the driver of the insured vehicle.
6. On the basis of the above pleadings following Issues were framed.

: I S S U E S:
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, she has sustained injuries on account of road traffic accident on 26-05-2023 at about 9.30 p.m. near KG Hospital, Thilaknagar road, Bangalore, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Car bearing Lily Mary vs Toshit Sanitation on 2 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/36732807/
2 Reg.No.KA-41-ME-1910?
2.
Whether the Petitioner is entitled for Compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
3. What order or Award ?
7.
In order to prove the case, the petitioner examined herself as PW.1 and one witness is examined as PW.2 and documents are got marked at Ex.P1 to Ex.P14.
The respondents have not adduced any oral evidence.

8. Heard arguments of the petitioner and respondents and perused the materials placed on record.
9.

My findings on the above-referred Issues are as under:-
 Issue No.1:- In the Affirmative.

Issue No.2:- In Partly Affirmative.
 Issue No.3:-

As per the final order,
 for the following.

:REASONS:
10. Issue No.1 : - In order to explain the actionable negligence of the driver of offending vehicle,
P.W.1 has filed her affidavit explaining the vivid picture of the accident that took place on 26-05-2023, at about 9-30 P.M when the petitioner was traveling as a pillion rider in Dio Scooter bearing Reg.No.KA-05/KM-0706, on Thilak Nagara main road, Bangalore and when they reached near K.G. Hospital, at that time, the driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA- 41/ME-1910 (hereinafter referred to as the offending the vehicle) drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's motor cycle, result of which the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
11.

In support of the claim and to prove the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle, the P.W.1 has relied upon Ex.P1 to 7 which are the police records such as FIR with complaint, spot mahazar, sketch, notice u/Sec. 133 of IMV Act and reply given there on, wound certificate, IMV report, charge sheet etc.,
12.

On the basis of the complaint lodged by Vinod Kumar, case has been registered against the driver of the offending vehicle in Crime No.0091/2023 of Mico Layout Traffic police Station for the offence punishable under section 279, 337 of IPC.

The Investigation officer after investigation has filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offences punishable under Section 279,
337 of IPC.
13. Respondents having filed written statement, not adduced either oral evidence or documentary evidence .

As per the police records and the evidence of PW-1 she was riding in the two wheeler Lily Mary vs Toshit Sanitation on 2 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/36732807/
3 referred above as pillion rider and they were proceeding towards Thilak Nagara Police Station from Swagath Junction.
The offending vehicle which came from the same direction from behind the vehicle of the petitioner hit against to the said vehicle on its rear side.
It is true that accident in question has occurred somewhere in the middle of the road.
But when both vehicles were proceeding on the same direction, had the driver of the offending vehicle maintained minimum distance this accident could have been avoided.
Hence, the material placed on record clearly proves that the driver of the offending vehicle has contributed sole negligence.
As observed supra the respondents have not adduced contra evidence in rebuttable of the evidence placed by the petitioner.
Hence, without discussing much on this point, this courts holds issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
14. Issue No.2:- The petitioner has given evidence to the effect of her sustained injures over her body.

Ex.P5 is the wound certificate issued from KG Hospital to the effect that petitioner has taken treatment in the said hospital for a period of 4 days and has been treated for three injuries which are simple in nature.

15. Mr. Punya Murthy C P -Medical Record Technician at KG Hospital, Bangalore is examined as PW.2 and through him Police intimation, MLC and case sheet are got marked as Ex.P12 to Ex.P14.
16.

The petitioner has not examined the medical officer who has given treatment to her and no evidence on record to say that she has suffered permanent disability, as such there is no any loss of future income.
Hence, petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the head of loss of future income.
17. Towards pain and sufferings, the petitioner shown to have sustained three simple injuries.

Hence taking in to consideration the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, time taken for treatment and sufferings during the treatment etc, it is reasonable to hold that petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.30,000/- towards pain and suffering.
19. Regarding treatment and medical expenses incurred etc, the petitioner has taken treatment at K G Hospital at Bangalore.
To that effect she has produced medical bills for Rs.25,500/- at Ex.P9.
Hence, petitioner is entitled for Rs.25,500/- under the head medical expenses.

20. Further for 4 days of hospitalization at K G Hospital at Bangalore and for her taking follow up treatment in the K G Hospital at Bangalore requires an attendant, was traveled to hospital for treatment, for follow-ups has incurred traveling expenses, she has taken nourishment and need further nourishment at this age and incurred other incidental expenses therefore all together incidental expenses is assessed at Rs.20,000/-.
21. It is submitted by the petitioner that she was doing coolie work and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.

Hence this court considering the age of the petitioner, the year of accident and place of residence of the petitioner considers the income of the petitioner as Rs.16,000/- p.m.
Lily Mary vs Toshit Sanitation on 2 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/36732807/
4 22.
The petitioner has sustained simple injuries and taken treatment for 4 days as an inpatient.
Hence the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner which is grievous in nature it is reasonable to hold that period of two months as complete laid down period.
Hence taking in to consideration the avocation of the petitioner and loss of income caused from said avocation this court takes the loss of income during laid down period for two months.
Hence petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.32,000/- towards loss of income during the laid down period.
23. The petitioner at her age of 60 years has suffered simple injuries.
Hence taking in to consideration the said aspect the petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.25,000/- towards loss of amenities and discomforts.

Thereby petitioner is entitled to the compensation as under:
Sl. Heads Amount No.
1. Towards pain and sufferings Rs. 30,000/-

2 . Towards Conveyance, Attendant Rs. 20,000/-
 charges and nourishing food

3. Medical expenses Rs. 25,500/-
4. Loss of income during laid down Rs. 32,000/-
 period 5. Loss of discomfort and amenities Rs. 25,000/-

Therefore this court holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,32,500/- (Rupees One Lakh Thirty Two Thousand Five Hundred only).
24.
As regarding liability is concerned, there is no dispute that offending vehicle was insured with 2nd respondent and policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Further the driver of offending vehicle had driving license to drive the offending vehicle.
Hence it can be said that all the documents pertaining to the vehicle in question was valid and in force as on the date of accident.

Hence by fastening liability on the respondent no.2 this court directs the respondent no.2 to pay compensation to the petitioner along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of accident till the date of payment of entire amount.
Accordingly Issue No. 2 is answered.
25. Issue No.3:
In the light of findings given on Issue No.1 and 2, my finding on this issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioner is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.1,32,500/- + cost of Rs.1,000/- imposed vide order on IA No.II & III.
The petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.1,33,500/- (Rupees One Lakh Thirty Three Thousand Five Hundred only).
